title: Moving a Factory MES to the Cloud Without Stopping Production
author: Kevin Wu
summary: Production lines run 24/7, so a big-bang migration is never an option. Here is the phased approach we use instead.

paragraphs: Manufacturing execution systems are some of the hardest systems to modernise. They are old, heavily customised, and the production line depends on them every minute of the day.
The good news is that you rarely need to replace the MES itself. Most of the value comes from moving the reporting and analytics layer around it.

body.heading: Start with reporting, not the core
paragraphs: We begin by building a cloud reporting layer that reads from the existing MES without changing it. The production line never notices.
bullets: Map every report and its data source
Replicate data to the cloud in near real time
Rebuild reports and verify them side by side

body.heading: Run old and new in parallel
paragraphs: Nothing is switched off until the client's own engineers have verified the new reports against the old ones. This takes weeks, not days, and it is worth it.
body.quote: The safest migration is the one where you can always go back.

title: What Hong Kong Fintechs Should Know About Cloud and Technology Risk
author: Grace Chan
summary: A practical overview of what regulators expect when you run financial services in the cloud.

paragraphs: Running financial services in the cloud is now normal in Hong Kong, but it comes with clear expectations around risk management, outsourcing and resilience.

body.heading: Questions to answer early
bullets: Where is customer data stored and processed?
Who can access production systems, and how is it logged?
How quickly can you recover from a cloud region outage?
How do you manage your technology vendors?
paragraphs: Answering these at the design stage costs far less than retrofitting them before an audit.

title: Building Bilingual (EN / 繁中) B2B Products: Lessons Learned
author: Mei Huang
summary: Translation is the easy part. Layout, search and data entry are where bilingual products really get hard.

paragraphs: Many B2B products in Taiwan and Hong Kong need to work equally well in English and Traditional Chinese. Here is what we have learned building them.

body.heading: Plan for it from day one
bullets: Keep all text out of the code from the first sprint
Test layouts with both languages, since text lengths differ a lot
Make search work across both scripts
Decide which fields customers can enter in either language
